subject: On the handling of empty data frames

messages.author: d3aaa07872b9962c
messages.subject: On the handling of empty data frames
parts:
Hi,

I often build plots with multiple layers, each layer using data from a
different data frame. Sometimes I need to make these plots in an
automated manner with for loops using data from different sources.
Sometimes some of these data frames are intentionally empty and I'm
always surprised how the plots turn out. Consider the following
example.

points = data.frame(x=1:5, y=1:5)
tiles = data.frame()

plot = (ggplot(points, aes(x, y))
+ geom_tile(data=tiles)
+ geom_point(data=points))

print(plot)

When tiles is empty, points, which is given as the argument to ggplot
is used as a fallback. Is this intentional? Why? I'd expect the
default behaviour when explicitly giving an empty data frame as an
argument to geom_* to be to plot nothing.

I know I could use an if-clause and test for nrow(tiles) > 0 or
something, but it would break the elegant single assignment code and I
wouldn't remember to anticipate the all emptiness anyway. Also, it
seems impossible to give an empty fallback data frame as an argument
to ggplot. Is there an easier way to avoid using fallback data than
adding if-clauses?

-- Osmo

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: On the handling of empty data frames
parts:
Hi Osmo,

This is a bug (http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/labels/data#issue/31)
- which is unfortunately a little tricky to fix.

However, it's not too hard to work around:

ggplot(points, aes(x, y)) +
(if (!empty(tiles)) geom_tile(data=tiles)) +
geom_point(data=points)

(this code won't work until ggplot 0.8.9)

Hadley
